q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most, and mid-size channels have the happiest audiences.

Outperformer rate (scored videos):
- Small: 35% (n=51 of 68 videos). Average lift is about 5.1x, which a few big hits may inflate.
- Mid: 24% (n=38).
- Large: 5% (n=19), about one video. Average lift is 0.9x.

Product-side net sentiment:
- Mid: +30 (52% positive, 22% negative, n=473 comments).
- Small: +21 (47% positive, 26% negative, n=762).
- Large: +9 (42% positive, 33% negative, n=319).

So small channels break out most and are fairly happy. Large channels rarely outperform and have the most mixed audiences. The large-channel sample is small, so treat that rate as directional. These are associations in a comment sample, not causes.
sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id,
    CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small'
         WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid'
         WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group,
    p.outperformer, p.rel_lift
  FROM content c
  JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
  JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
perf AS (
  SELECT size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_videos,
    SUM(outperformer IS NOT NULL) AS n_scored_videos,
    ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift
  FROM v GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group,
    COUNT(*) AS n_product_side_comments,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative,
    ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM v
  JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0
    AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT perf.size_group, n_videos, n_scored_videos, outperformer_rate, mean_rel_lift,
  n_product_side_comments,
  CASE WHEN n_product_side_comments>=10 THEN pct_positive END AS pct_positive,
  CASE WHEN n_product_side_comments>=10 THEN pct_negative END AS pct_negative,
  CASE WHEN n_product_side_comments>=10 THEN net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.size_group=perf.size_group
ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. They have the largest sample (n=18 videos), an average relative lift of 2.31, and 44% of videos outperformed their baseline. Sentiment is also solid at +35 (54% positive, 19% negative, n=240 product-side comments).

No other format beat its baseline reliably:
- Explainer/tips (n=6): lift 1.12, 17% outperformed, sentiment +9 (n=81).
- Comparison (n=3): lift 1.70 but 0% outperformed, sentiment +13 (n=48).
- Upgrade advice (n=6): lift 0.63, 0% outperformed, though sentiment was +46 (n=59).
- Keynote recap (n=2): lift 0.60, sentiment +9 (n=23).
- Other (n=3): lift 0.53, sentiment +77 (n=22).

Caveat: every format except first impressions has very few videos, so treat those rankings as tentative. These are associations, not proof of cause.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), perf AS (SELECT format, count(*) AS n_videos, count(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, round(avg(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, round(avg(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate FROM v GROUP BY format), sent AS (SELECT v.format, count(*) AS n_product_side, round(avg(cm.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, round(avg(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, round(avg(cm.sentiment='positive')-avg(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM v JOIN comments cm ON cm.video_id=v.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT perf.format, perf.n_videos, perf.n_with_baseline, perf.avg_rel_lift, perf.outperformer_rate, COALESCE(sent.n_product_side,0) AS n_product_side, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.pct_positive END AS pct_positive, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.pct_negative END AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side>=10 THEN sent.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent ON sent.format=perf.format ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC, perf.avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Among top-quartile-lift videos, none is clearly negative. The two lowest net sentiment scores are only neutral to slightly positive.

1. iJustine, "First impressions" video: net sentiment 0 (38.5% positive, 38.5% negative, n=13). Lift is 17.3, about 3.2x relative lift.

2. Shannon Grixti, "most impressive foldable yet" video: net sentiment +6 (41.2% positive, 35.3% negative, n=17). Lift is 84.78, about 6.0x relative lift.

Both samples are small, with 13 and 17 product-side comments. The sentiment gaps between these and the next videos (+7 and +17) are tiny, so the ranking could easily change. Lift and sentiment are also measured separately, so this doesn't show that either one drives the other.
sql: SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.lift, p.rel_lift, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY c.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC LIMIT 5

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Largest topics overall: Praise for the video (n=206, 9.4% of comments), Samsung Fold comparisons (n=140, 6.4%), Cases and design (n=112, 5.1%), and Eager to buy (n=103, 4.7%).

Fastest growing this week:
- Samsung Fold comparisons is the standout among big topics, rising from 15 to 67 comments (+52, about 3.5x).
- Cases and design rose from 17 to 55 (+38).
- Praise for the video rose from 29 to 69 (+40).
- Buy or don't buy (6 to 33) and Left-handed concerns (4 to 22) each grew about 4.5x.
- Apple Pencil support (1 to 12) and Fold animation (1 to 7) show the biggest percentage jumps.

Caveat: the Apple Pencil and Fold animation jumps start from a base of 1 comment, so they are small-n and shouldn't be over-read. Samsung Fold comparisons is the most meaningful riser.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT max(d) AS m FROM base), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, count(*) AS n_total, sum(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, sum(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM base, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, a.n_total, round(a.n_total*1.0/(SELECT count(*) FROM base),3) AS share_of_all_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week AS abs_change, round((a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)*1.0/nullif(a.n_prev_week,0),3) AS growth_vs_prev_week, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo has the most positive audience sentiment among the larger groups, with a net score of +22 (n=1,554 product-side comments across 126 videos). About 48% of those comments are positive and 26% negative.

- Event general videos: -20 net (n=86, 8 videos), with 24% positive and 44% negative.
- Other topics: -10 net (n=52, 6 videos), with 33% positive and 42% negative.
- Competitor foldables: +13 net (n=24, 2 videos), with 38% positive and 25% negative. This is very small, so treat it as a rough indication only.

Duo's lead over the event and other groups looks clear. Those groups have far fewer comments than Duo, so their scores are less stable. The data is a sample of comments, and official videos are excluded.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Commenters like the fold animation most clearly (net +70, n=56; 84% positive, 14% negative). Excitement to buy is also strong (net +38, n=103) and so are pre-order plans (net +52, n=52). By like ranking, Samsung Fold comparisons come first (net +31, n=140), then cases and design (net +25, n=112).

The most criticism sits in the same Samsung comparison topic (25% negative), followed by weighing the Duo against the iPhone 18 Pro Max (net +2, n=101; 32% negative) and high price (net +17, n=100; 31% negative). Left-handed concerns are the only net-negative topic (-8, n=37; 40% negative), though that sample is small.

Caveat: these are topics from a sample of comments, and comments can touch several topics, so treat them as patterns, not causes.
sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.sentiment
  FROM comments cm
  JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id = cm.video_id
  WHERE ct.topic = 'duo' AND ct.format != 'official'
    AND cm.lang = 'en' AND cm.trivial = 0
    AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
    AND cm.topic_id IS NOT NULL
), agg AS (
  SELECT topic_id,
         COUNT(*) AS n_comments,
         SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos,
         SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg,
         SUM(sentiment='neutral') AS n_neu
  FROM c GROUP BY topic_id
)
SELECT t.name, t.summary, a.n_comments, a.n_pos, a.n_neg, a.n_neu,
       ROUND(1.0*a.n_pos/a.n_comments,3) AS pos_share,
       ROUND(1.0*a.n_neg/a.n_comments,3) AS neg_share,
       ROUND(1.0*(a.n_pos-a.n_neg)/a.n_comments,3) AS net_sentiment,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_pos DESC) AS rank_liked,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY a.n_neg DESC) AS rank_criticised
FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = a.topic_id
WHERE t.pool = 'product'
ORDER BY a.n_comments DESC
LIMIT 40
